ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The vertical axis of the PES spectrum is Relative Number of Electrons, and the horizontal axis is Binding Energy (MJ/mol). The binding energies marked on the peaks in the figure include, in order, 104, 6.84, 4.98, 2.29, and 1.76 MJ/mol. Reasoning: When photoelectrons are irradiated by the same light source, the kinetic energy relationship is KE = hν − binding energy. Because hν is the same, the smaller the binding energy, the greater the kinetic energy after ejection; the greater the kinetic energy, the greater the speed as well. Among the marked binding energies, the smallest is 1.76 MJ/mol, so the electrons from the 1.76 MJ/mol peak have the greatest speed after ejection.

raw_record.question_text:

Use the PES spectra below to answer questions.

method.method_draft: First inspect the PES spectrum and list the binding energies printed above the peaks. Then apply the photoelectron energy relationship KE = hν − binding energy. Since all peaks are measured with the same photon source, compare only the binding energies: the smallest binding energy gives the largest kinetic energy and thus largest velocity. The smallest labeled binding energy is 1.76 MJ/mol, so the electron from the 1.76 MJ/mol peak has the greatest velocity after ejection.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：PES 光谱的纵轴是 Relative Number of Electrons，横轴是 Binding Energy (MJ/mol)。图中峰上标出的结合能依次包括 104、6.84、4.98、2.29 和 1.76 MJ/mol。推理：光电子被同一光源照射时，动能关系为 KE = hν − binding energy。因为 hν 相同，结合能越小，逸出后的动能越大；动能越大，速度也越大。标出的结合能中最小的是 1.76 MJ/mol，所以来自 1.76 MJ/mol 峰的电子逸出后速度最大。

method.CoT_qualify_0: 无需修改。该推理先描述图像中的坐标轴与峰值标签，再基于同一光源下 KE = hν − binding energy 判断最小结合能对应最大动能和最大速度，结论与标准答案一致。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct physics route using the photoelectric energy balance and the labeled binding energies in the spectrum; this is the natural single solution path for the problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the PES graph and identify the labeled peak binding energies: 104, 6.84, 4.98, 2.29, and 1.76 MJ/mol. Note that 1.76 MJ/mol is the smallest binding-energy peak shown, at the far right of the spectrum.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording to determine that it asks for the peak whose ejected electron has the greatest velocity, not the tallest peak or the greatest number of electrons.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the PES/photoelectric relation: for electrons ejected by the same incident photon energy, kinetic energy after ejection equals photon energy minus binding energy. Greater kinetic energy means greater speed, so the electron with the lowest binding energy will have the greatest velocity.
